title: Undo/Redo State Machine with History Stack
problemStatement: Implement `createUndoRedo(initialPresent)` supporting `set(newPresent)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `canUndo()`, and `canRedo()`. Setting a new value clears the future stack.
interviewTrap: A common bug is forgetting to clear the future/redo stack when a new mutation is made after an undo, resulting in corrupted parallel history timelines.

testCases.name: Performs basic undo and restores previous state
testCases.testFn: const hist = createUndoRedo(0); hist.set(1); hist.set(2); hist.undo(); return hist.present;

testCases.name: New mutation after undo clears the redo stack
testCases.input: undo, then set 3 -> canRedo must be false
testCases.testFn: const hist = createUndoRedo(0); hist.set(1); hist.undo(); hist.set(99); return hist.canRedo();

testCases.name: Redo restores undone state
testCases.testFn: const hist = createUndoRedo(0); hist.set(1); hist.undo(); hist.redo(); return hist.present;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: The State Reducer pattern allows the consumer of a custom hook to intercept and customize state transitions before they are committed, giving developers total control without modifying hook internals.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Immutable History State Reducer.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Immutable History State Reducer maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal
